item.description:
• Two can pass on one tile, never through each other: a body is solid at its tile's middle, the way past runs along the edge; room rules written down: one doorway kept clear, fixtures along the walls, the sign in the far corner
  • Nothing sits in a doorway: beds keep off the dorm's door cell and the bath's fixtures off its door and sign; a walk whose only way is past someone waits on them instead of finding no way; the Bath press picks like the Workout press
  • The Workout press takes whoever is resting: a lounger first, then a quiet worker still counted busy, then a sleeping teammate; a turn in the gym is not cut short by a session refresh re-planning rest
  • Faster feedback from GitHub: the board's delta, the feed as a doorbell, asks that expect a change
  • The gym: a room off the living cluster, four fixtures, a turn that lasts its whole time
  • A crate is a merged pull request: the rule as a check, the pull request asked by number
  • A teammate's pull request that leaves the open list is asked whether it merged or closed
  • The pallet's state has one home, every crate has a number, and the architecture notes are checked
  • Leftovers off the floor, and the audit says what the code says
  • A carry names a yard; the place is asked for on the way and remembered on the row
  • One truth per crate: where the station has it joins its ledger row
  • Truth before the picture, a carrier that hurries, and the reconciler per crate
  • Station time is one value, and a route no longer rebuilds the yard on every step
  • One crate ledger: the source's word and the station's, per crate, and the counts read off it
  • The scenarios judge the run as it happened, not as it was worded
  • The two truth scenarios name a crate the way the floor does: an unnumbered one is "a crate"
  • Station truth outlasts a source that runs behind: hand landings by yard, one rule for what a yard holds, the reconciler out of the redraw, a redraw that adopts its nodes
  • A deck over capacity spreads a repository's crates over its own columns rather than one tower
  • Haul progress is read off the crates, not kept in flags: a merged office clears when its package's placement says it is down in the yard; the deck reconciler waits on carried crates
  • A merged office clears when its crate lands in storage, not when it is picked up; a checkout that goes away mid-haul waits for the haul; a haul to storage survives the office closing
  • A click on any part of a crate opens its pull request: the hit resolves to the named prop
  • Repository colours come from the name, the same on every launch; the build stamp lives in About
  • The app menu says which commit the build came from
  • A wonder beat with a walk ahead is still a walk: the pallet errand begins at the console, not where the order came; cones are not in the way of their own row; a walk never ends on a cell with something standing on its middle
  • One cone per session: the message being worked, queued ones in a row behind it, the old one shrinks away; repository names kept with the board so the deck is drawn right from launch; the world's diff runs before the redraw so a cleared crate is carried from where it stood
  • A pallet errand is a job nothing calls the operator away from; whoever adopts one stands beside it; cones owed to an office land with its reveal; scenarios can forbid lines
  • Shuttle flies on the station clock; the simulator's board catch-up waits on it too; a commit is stowed as a cube by command; the first release answer is quiet
  • A pull request newly open on my checkout is announced from the poll's state change, so the office's worker packs it; an approach walks to the stand cell once and shuffles from there
  • Carries approach on foot and never from on top of the slot; a pull request is packed by the office's worker; a pallet with no operator gets one; the pusher walks round the pallet
  • Offices unfold from the hex at the doorway and roll back up on close; airlock is a 2x2 chamber with working doors; rocket loads through a hatch
  • Solid: minions solid to each other, wait then walk round; inner lanes off the walls; walks re-planned when the floor changes; spawns spread into their offices
  • STATION.md: an office closes by rolling up into a hex
  • Orders: one entry point, a visible beat on a change of orders, phases that advance, a visit that lasts, fixtures reserved, no coin tosses; station time for patience and reactions; a merged office clears when its haul is done; the suite steps station time and runs in under a minute
  • One table moves every crate's picture, on the station clock: no scene action moves a crate any more
  • The rocket check fires at the climb; chores never stand on a buried cell
  • Things are heavy: one lift, one set-down, and no empty launches
  • STATION.md: the crate shrinks into the hold
  • STATION.md: rockets are loaded at the foot; a moving pallet is solid
  • An invariant checker and a scripted scenario suite
  • STATION.md: the office unfolds from its crate at the doorway
  • STATION.md: no shared spots even at the start, lanes clear of walls, the office ripples out from its crate
  • Audit every command and cue against the rulebook
  • STATION.md: a change of orders is visible
  • The airlock stands in the corridor's line before the bay; the monolith answers with cones of light; crate plates are lights, off in the yard; the idle drift to the pad when a rocket steams
  • STATION.md: answers from the interview
  • The shower happens under the nozzle for its whole ten seconds; pace by task; QA inspects the stacks, not the floor
  • The pallet is heavy: it is shoved one axis at a time
  • STATION.md: what things are, what they may do, what may move them
  • Every crate keeps its yard slot until it leaves; the pixel patch draws on top of the body; the board button says where it moves the issue; lightning only at the monolith
  • Simulator: reset on its own line
  • Simulator: a Reset org button that starts the station over
  • Rebuild the simulator panel around one target office
  • Simulator: a new session's branch goes in the chosen office's repository
  • Simulator: issue numbers per repository, and the new-session button says which repo it uses
  • A teammate's pull request is a crate with its sticker, not cubes; the office hex keeps its turn on the arms and waits for the ship to lift; the simulator tells a new branch from a pull request
  • The staging pallet
  • Shuttles, rockets and the crew run commands too
  • Closed is not merged: a red crate that fades with the office; one merged event per merge; the rocket waits for crates still on someone's arms
  • Carry polish: one crate size, set-down by level (crouch, slide, over the head, hop), the crate stays on the arms until its slot and nothing moves it after
  • Split Scene.swift by reason to change
  • Carries know the stack: top-down pickup, height-aware postures
  • A simulator: the whole pipeline driven by hand, with every event and command in the log
  • Spec: a crate is heavy, nothing moves it after release
  • Spec: one crate size, no spin on release
  • Spec: set-down postures per stack level, still owed
  • Spec: set-down postures per stack level
  • Spec: closed, not merged
  • Pallet spec: impatient dispatcher, telekinetic loading and unloading, a bobbing pallet pushed to the deck
  • Commands as values and station truth: minions run one command at a time with interruptible phases; completions write station truth; hover pauses a minion and shows its orders
  • Architecture map: where this is going (facts, authority, commands, station truth)
  • Split the data layer out of the scene into World
  • A crate set down in storage by hand stays until the source counts it
  • Cleanup round: per-repository readiness (no shuttles for a late first answer), a WorldEvent seam between diffs and cues, ARCHITECTURE.md
  • Shower as a wall nozzle and a drain, clear of the sign; a low coffee table
  • Cubes only where they mean something: a slab table on legs, flat tick and portholes; furniture blocks the floor
  • A blocky plant: square pot, thin stem, flat leaves
  • Nothing round: every turned shape gets four or six flat sides, spheres become cubes
  • The bay is outside: with an airlock against it, everyone comes in and goes out through the hatch
  • Own tempo and tool rota per minion, chores for loungers, sooner bath visits, an airlock by the bay that departures leave through
  • No cone for an office that is gone (crash); a covered cone is worked from the cell beside it; a retarget never leaves the room
  • Couch and bed pulls leave minions on errands alone; a carrier gives up its seat; a walker with no path walks straight rather than sliding
  • The yard follows GitHub through the minions: crates the board moved to staging are carried across, counts snap only for the rest; the staging haul finds its crates again
  • Night is the clock's business alone: a quiet afternoon is spent in the lounge, not in bed
  • A merged office stays retired while its session lingers; the minion waits in the lounge instead of rebuilding it every scan
  • Updates re-plan rather than reset: settled minions stay, walkers keep their destination; core tiles stop replaying their build; couches drawn by wall, not by index
  • Crates are carried to the slot the yard layout will give them, so nothing jumps on landing; lifting is a crouch with the crate passing the chest
  • Dorm and bath placed beside the lounge, existing layouts re-clustered; one minion to a couch
  • Rules for idleness: read on the couch by day, sleep by night, showers after long work, pees after short, loungers now and then
  • The bath's pixel patch sits where it should; a visit is a pee at the bowl or a shower under falling pixels
  • Doorways through the yard, a bath with pixel static, a livelier lounge, my name on my offices
  • Tested crates nearest the pad, crates grouped by repository in stacks of three
  • Deck split into an untested row and a tested row; a tested crate is carried across; status plate on the side, approved sticker on the lid
  • Latest release notes in the app menu: What's New shows the notes bundled with the build
  • Bold black ink on tiles, boxes and cones keep off the writing and inside their tile
  • No board offices before GitHub has said who I am
  • An office already on the floor is no proof of work; only peers' claims and checkouts are
  • Dark ink on tiles, names as floor signage, open pull requests only, no archive flapping
  • Board column decides an office's solidity, not its existence; board state persists across launches
  • Yard and cues from the GitHub project board, offices for issues in development, release notes from commits
  • Translucent feet under props, the office hex without a plane, cones land clear of crates near the door
  • A cell under a crate is no destination: walks settle for the nearest free floor
  • Minions walk round crates, boxes and pyramids on a finer grid; aisles through storage and the deck
  • PR marker is the square strapped crate again; hex stays the packed office
  • Kick offices, honest sharing light, crates with stickers carried by hand, hammer and flashlight, boxes away from the door
  • Peers share parsed GitHub answers so one poll serves the room; README on sharing
  • Peers share offices by branch onto one work station instead of standing beside it
  • Fold the crew station into the work station: teammates' branches share offices with local checkouts
  • Cursor-centred zoom, two-finger pan, drag tilt, WASD/QE camera keys, station hotkeys 0-4
  • Readable labels on small offices, no closets against the hallway, calm settings changes
  • Smaller odd-sized offices, 4x2 bay across the south arm
  • Squarer fleet, yard along the west side, cursor-pivot rotate, snappy panning
  • Yard in a line with 4x4 storage, staging and pad; couches and a standing crew; loading on clearance with steam; impatient tester
  • Worker crew: free workers are reused, shuttles bring more, extras fade when bunks are full
  • Pyramids move with their station and vanish with their office
  • Production branch per repository: configured, else main, else master
  • Prompt pyramids only in offices
  • Exact staging/production diff from git; clickable crates; minion shadows; bunk beds with lounge overflow
  • Sci-fi tools: flat goggles, tablet, scanner, forward-held hammer; testing sweeps instead of spinning
  • Repair cargo detection: only repositories with a real release pipeline, thirty-day floor
  • Cargo only for repositories with a real release pipeline; thirty-day floor
  • Game-style pyramids with feet, crate packages, minion tools, more distinct routines
  • Graphics gallery window: every prop and animation on a labelled tile
  • Wider repo palette; a spinner beside a repo title while it refreshes from GitHub
  • Bounded room placement; share repositories individually, nothing shared by default
  • Larger launch pad, storage yard and test deck
  • Fix a render-thread spin when a queued message has no room to put its cone in
  • One package per pull request; storage and deck from GitHub; proper rising; cone spots; lounge; archive cancels hauls
  • Sharing indicator in the HUD
  • Bonjour peers: share stations on the local network
  • Rockets grow with cargo; faint rings on the pad when a release is due
  • Storage keeps repo colours; rockets load only their own repo's boxes
  • One cone per message; queued messages show as dim cones
  • Uncommitted work shows as translucent boxes; minions stand beside the cone and bend from the feet
  • CI status pulses red; stale rooms gather dust; haul thuds; welding, hammering, pushing and bending at the cone
  • Rooms persist and lose power instead of vanishing; room-coloured prompt cones; three box sizes; storage bay with merge hauling and rocket loading; steadier settings layout
  • Settings window: station rule, per-repo station and crew overrides, people names, general options
  • Configurable station rule; updater only inside a bundle and never headless
  • Work station by GitHub owner, configurable; works without Conductor
  • README: homage to rymdkapsel
  • Rename to rumkapsel
  • Update notice in the station log; feature request and bug report menu items
  • Sparkle updates, Developer ID signing and notarisation in the release script
  • Float on top is a remembered preference, off by default; launch in the background
  • Bolder condensed signage without tracking
  • Signage tucked into room corners
  • Uppercase signage in room accent colours; release script
  • Clean tile borders, centred short labels, crew display names, stale merged rooms archived, corridor growth, activity-driven music layers
  • A failed open-PR fetch is not an empty list
  • Workspace rooms live while the Conductor folder exists; scan two weeks of transcripts
  • Dark rooms keep their repo colour, just dimmed
  • Simple room ladder: dark until a branch, lit after; boxes only for commits
  • PR implies pushed; unlaid tiles are a dark subfloor
  • Rooms fill in tile by tile with branch progress; no dashed outlines
  • Crew counts as loaded only once every repo has answered
  • Commits counted against develop; local branches are placeholders until pushed; minions carry new commit boxes in
  • Shuttles arrive from random corners with a yaw drift; crate lifts smoothly onto the minion
  • Crew offices only for PRs touched in the last two weeks
  • Crew station goes live: open PRs as offices, pushes as boxes, only fresh events animate
  • Crew from the repository events feed; bots bay; work-crew bridge; anchored slow shuttle landings with hex crates; merged branches leave
  • Crew station: teammates' pull requests replayed over the day; archive animation; crew focus key
  • Branchless sessions get a grey placeholder office; branch creation orders the real one
  • Eight beds; overflow sleepers lie in the hallway
  • Minions sleep as long as their office stands
  • Star field, untested releases hold on the pad with tape and gantry, QA sessions inspect the rocket
  • Strict doorway crossing; per-activity working animations
  • Resolve worktrees to the main checkout; one release root per repo; refresh on focus
  • Clicking a minion refreshes its repo on GitHub
  • Cooler centred rocket, releases for all Conductor repos, no SpriteKit shape nodes
  • Slow lift-off; staging rocket yields to production
  • G refreshes GitHub on demand
  • Launch pad with release rockets, more robust PR lookup, PR state change log
  • Keep PR status colours distinct on boxes
  • Room-tinted boxes with flat shading and floor shadows
  • Doorways as open edges in the border, like the game
  • Doorways, in-place office renames, sway/jump/pace animations, cluttered commit boxes
  • Remove orphaned construction outlines
  • Hangar at the outer south arm, offices delivered by ship
  • Render-thread mutation, FSEvents scanning, lightning, commit boxes, label collisions
